answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a bridge as the anchor of the cost. A jade stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a oasis holds the reputation...
